subject: Renewal: capacity uplift & overflow handling — NimbusAI
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@nimbusai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Tasha Moreno <tasha.moreno@nimbusai.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity uplift request

Hi Evelyn,

Hope you had a good week. We're starting our renewal planning and want to propose an uplift to our dedicated pool for the coming term. Over the last quarter our inference volume grew ~2.6x (mostly peak bursts during nightly batch transforms) and our current reserved pool is hitting saturation frequently.

High-level ask: add 40 reserved GPUs to our pool (bringing us from 20 to 60), plus a written throughput target (p95 token latency and per-minute throughput) for the committed capacity. If we move to a 24-month commit we can probably negotiate pricing.

On overflow: we prefer automatic spillover to on-demand rather than hard throttling, but we want clear billing caps or credits if overflow spends spike unexpectedly. Can you send an options matrix with pricing and an operational plan (how traffic is routed, what triggers spillover, and expected latency changes)?

cc: Tasha (procurement) to keep them in the loop.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, NimbusAI

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Tasha Moreno <tasha.moreno@nimbusai.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift request

Samir — thanks for the detail and the heads-up. We're glad NimbusAI is scaling. Quick summary of what I can put together for you this week:

- Two capacity options: +40 GPUs (60 total) as a single reserved pool, or +20 GPUs now and +20 mid-term (12mo point) with staged provisioning.
- Term choices: 12mo (standard) or 24mo (discounted unit rate).
- Throughput/SLA: we can commit to a per-pool p95 token-latency target under steady-state load; we'll provide a draft SLA section for the amendment.
- Overflow strategies: three approaches we recommend:
  * Hard cap: stop serving beyond reserved capacity (simplest, predictable billing = no overflow).
  * On-demand spillover: route excess to on-demand nodes at a higher per-token rate; automatically kicks in when queue times exceed X ms or pool concurrency threshold reached.
  * Hybrid (preferred): on-demand spillover with a monthly overflow credit bucket and a soft throttle at very high sustained usage.

Ben (sales) — can you prepare pricing for the three approaches + the staged-provisioning schedule? Soojin — can you advise on wording for the SLA/billing carve-outs and any compliance notes we should add for data residency?

Samir/Tasha — any constraints on procurement timing or procurement review boards we should be aware of?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>, Samir Shah <samir@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Tasha Moreno <tasha.moreno@nimbusai.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift request (pricing options)

Samir / Evelyn — attaching an initial pricing matrix (see attachments). High level:

- Option A (Hard cap): +40 GPUs, 12mo term: $XX,XXX/month. No overflow billing; requests beyond cap return 429s.
- Option B (On-demand spillover): +40 GPUs, 12mo term: $YY,YYY/month + overflow billed at 2.5x hosted on-demand rate.
- Option C (Hybrid w/credit bucket): +40 GPUs, 12mo term: $ZZ,ZZZ/month including 50 GPU-hours of spillover credit per month; overflow beyond credits billed at 1.8x hosted rate.

Discounts: 10% for 24mo on top of listed rates.

Operational notes:
- For on-demand spillover we recommend: automatic routing when pool concurrency > 80% for >= 60s, and a queue depth trigger.
- Canary ramp: when new GPUs added we stage traffic over 72hrs and monitor p95 latency + error rate.
- Billing behavior: we can add a 30-day "first-term grace" where overflow billing is capped to forecasted baseline for the first month post-upgrade, per your ask.

Evelyn — sending the amendment draft next. Samir/Tasha — flag any finance constraints.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>, Samir Shah <samir@nimbusai.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift request (SLA and operational language)

Hi all — adding a few technical/legal clarifications to make the amendment robust:

1) SLA wording: when we commit a p95 token latency for the reserved pool, we need an explicit definition of measurement windows (daily 1hr windows vs rolling 30d) and an inclusion/exclusion for planned maintenance and tenant-isolation incidents.

2) Spillover behavior: suggest defining two tiers of overflow:
   - Soft overflow: automatic routing to on-demand up to N concurrent jobs per minute; latency expectations documented as a separate non-SLA metric (expected +X–Y ms).
   - Hard overflow: escalation to support if sustained > 20% of total monthly tokens for 24 hours. This triggers a capacity review and potential emergency scaling but is not an automatic billing suspension.

3) Billing guardrails: include a monthly cap option that Nimbus can opt into (absolute dollar cap or absolute token cap) and an alerting cadence (email + Slack) when projected overflow spend exceeds 50% of the cap.

4) Implementation notes: KV-cache warmup and prefix caching reduce spillover cost; we recommend a pre-warm job and a 48hr traffic-shaping window after upgrade. We'll capture these as runbook steps in the amendment.

Attached: suggested SLA clause snippets (I will paste into the draft PDF). Also linking HubSpot deal and DocuSign for signatures.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@nimbusai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Tasha Moreno <tasha.moreno@nimbusai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift request

Evelyn / Ben / Soojin — thanks, this is helpful. A few quick confirmations: 

- Nimbus prefers the Hybrid (credit bucket) option with the 24mo discount if we can get the 30-day first-term grace on overflow billing documented. That should give our SREs runway.
- Please include explicit language that soft overflow will not be used to retroactively bill historical traffic (we want predictable billing windows).
- We accept the proposed canary ramp and pre-warm steps; please include them in the runbook.

Tasha — procurement is happy to proceed with the 24mo amendment once we have the finalized draft and DocuSign link.

If you can circulate the finalized amendment (PDF + DocuSign) by EOD Wed the 12th that would keep us on target for a Sept 1st renewal start.

Best,
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, NimbusAI
